notes: South Dakota has no personal income tax, so self-employment income is subject only to federal income and self-employment tax.

South Dakota's 4.2% state sales tax (plus any municipal sales tax) applies to sales of services unless a specific exemption applies, so many freelancers must collect and remit sales tax; this is a pass-through tax on customers and is not modeled.

seDeduction.note: Not applicable: South Dakota has no personal income tax.

seHealthInsurance.note: Not applicable: South Dakota has no personal income tax.

retirementContributions.note: Not applicable: South Dakota has no personal income tax.

qbi.note: Not applicable: South Dakota has no personal income tax.

localIncomeTax.note: South Dakota cities and counties do not levy a local income tax.

estimatedTax.threshold: Not applicable: no state personal income tax.

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $150 Articles of Organization filed online ($165 on paper) with the South Dakota Secretary of State.
businessCosts.annualReportFee: $55 annual report filed online ($70 on paper), due every year; $55 late fee if delinquent.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: None. South Dakota has no corporate, unitary or personal income tax and no franchise tax on LLCs.
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: None for a typical freelancer. (Contractor's excise tax of 2% applies only to construction services; municipal gross receipts tax applies only to alcohol, eating establishments, lodging and admissions.)
